description: The full Phase 1 author packet. Arms A-E receive exactly this directory and read nothing outside it.
notes: Every file carries a prepended provenance header (an HTML comment). `kind` describes the body below that header: `verbatim-whole-file`, `verbatim-extract`, or `assembled` (a stub written for this packet, reproducing nothing from the document it stands in for).
MANIFEST.json is not listed among its own files.
PHASE_1_AUTHOR_BRIEF.md §3.1 points at `src/contract/PERCEPTION_VERDICT.md`; in this packet that file is at `catalog/src/contract/PERCEPTION_VERDICT.md`.

`mayContainCampaignConclusions` is a leakage flag against the brief's §7 promise that authors receive no failure analyses and no instrument conclusions. It is acted on, not merely recorded: `trim` lists what was removed and why, `keptDespiteFlag` lists what was flagged and kept and why.

files.note: The brief itself. §2 quotes the incumbent's measured failures (72.8% re-encode agreement, a ±1-LSB dither moving all 114 test palettes, ~900 tunable sites against 11 anchors, 1.61× overfitting) and §3.1 carries perception-4's measured thresholds and the 0.750/0.361 accent result. Sanctioned: §2 states outright that these numbers 'are here because they define the target'. Delivered as-is — the brief is frozen.

§6.1 carries the SAM determinism measurement (144 inferences, 5,148 regions, zero differing bytes) and the ~6.2 s cold-call cost. Sanctioned: PHASE_1_AUTHOR_BRIEF.md §3.1 already states both and cites §6.1 for them. §7, §7.1 and §8 have been removed — see the `trim` block.

States v2-3's 72.8% re-encode palette agreement and the ±1-LSB dither moving all 114 test palettes. Kept: both figures are already in PHASE_1_AUTHOR_BRIEF.md §2 verbatim and deliberately, so re-reading them here tells an author nothing §2 did not. Removing them would be theatre.

Its worked example is a real study result rather than an invented one: the gap-scan at p 0.2927 corrected against 0.0172 raw on the same 43 items. Kept: it is a methodology illustration about multiplicity correction and concludes nothing about any palette approach.

States the standing v3-era evidence position ("zero standing palette verdicts") and legacy tier-overlap counts (31 keys, 9 strong-graded-acceptable). Kept: these are inventory facts about the evidence store, of the kind PHASE_1_AUTHOR_BRIEF.md §4 already gives in more detail, and no palette approach is judged in them.

Cites v2-3's parameter-honesty findings as calibration context: roughly 900 tunable sites against 11 human anchors, and a 1.61× overfitting alarm against a target of ~1.0. Kept: all three figures are in PHASE_1_AUTHOR_BRIEF.md §2 verbatim and deliberately.

A measurement result by nature — perception-4's thresholds, ratios, refusals and the signed-off disposition. Largely the sanctioned overlap with PHASE_1_AUTHOR_BRIEF.md §3.1, which summarises the same round and names this file canonical. It does exceed §3.1 in three places §3.1 does not touch: the full per-region same-colour bar table (0.00932 / 0.01502 / 0.01627 / 0.02293), POOLED_SAME_COLOR_BAR and the P1 excursion multiplier (2.5×), and the invariant-3 adoption cost. All three are contract internals rather than conclusions about any palette paradigm.

trim.removed: §7 (Measured resolution floors, ladder-sample-1), §7.1 (re-scored against a capped answer key — what survives and what does not) and §8 (Open items): source lines 604 to 807.
trim.reason: Instrument conclusions and an open-items ledger. The brief's §3 table makes §§1-5 normative and cites §6/§6.1; §7 onward was never promised to an author, and PHASE_1_AUTHOR_BRIEF.md §7 withholds the instruments' conclusions.
trim.danglingCrossReference: One kept line now points at withheld text: §6's "What is still open: which model runs the bulk pass. See §8." (source line 513). The body is verbatim so it was not edited; the provenance header at the top of the packet copy states that §7, §7.1 and §8 are withheld and how to ask for them, which is where a reader who follows that pointer lands.

trim.reason: States measured results about the review channel as findings — what past rounds produced (all 14 gradient notes asked for more gradient with no way to record the opposite objection; 5 of 19 endorsed accents reachable) and what an earlier review design got wrong. Also not author-relevant: an author designing a palette algorithm does not need the review channel internals, so the stub costs the phase close to nothing.

Reports measured adversarial-unblinding results against the review channel (24/24 via the gradient field; pre-salt-fix, all 120 palette hashes reconstructed, 28 of 60 items unblinded with certainty). Also not author-relevant: an author designing a palette algorithm does not need the review server internals, so the stub costs the phase close to nothing.

Reports measured oracle accuracy and agreement as findings: ground_type exact match 23% (variant A) against 53% (variant B), κ 0.21-0.31, and a pre-registered replication recorded FAILED. One arm is seated on a parse-then-assign route; telling that author the semantic route measures weak could kill the paradigm before it is written, which is the precise failure mode Phase 1 exists to prevent. This is a real cost and the stub says so. PARTIALLY RESTORED: catalog/ORACLE_QUESTION_INVENTORY.md carries the ids, vocabularies and question wording extracted from this document, with everything on the what-it-found side removed — see oracleQuestionInventory.

§7 presents measured corpus-survey results as findings (0.00% of images exceed 768 px; filename prefixes predict rendition size; §7.2, 644 artworks present in both resolution tiers), alongside the oracle pipeline architecture. Withheld with its companion so that the oracle is described to an author by its §5 catalog row alone rather than by half of its documentation. This is a real cost and the stub says so.

oracleQuestionInventory.why: The §5 catalog row describes the oracle as 'a VLM question set' without saying what it asks. Which questions exist is on the WHAT IT MEASURES side of the brief's own line, so a bare stub was withholding something the brief promised. This file restores that and nothing else.
idOnly: ground_type (as a derived output of the probe instrument)
field_texture (as a derived output of the probe instrument)
shading_geometry (as a derived output of the probe instrument)
shading_direction (the source states its vocabulary only by reference to another field)
oracleQuestionInventory.stripped: Everything on the what-it-found side: per-question accuracy and exact-match rates, inter-variant and human agreement, kappas, the A/B/C/D prompt-variant comparisons and their replication verdict, per-field reliability grades and [UNCALIBRATED]/[MEASURED] tags, resolution-tier floors, unmapped-answer shares, sign-off and adoption status, the derivation table for the probe arm, the changelog, both appendices, and every design rule the source says was earned by a measurement. The whole "decision it feeds" column of every group table was dropped rather than filtered, because six of its cells carry v2-3 failure analyses or measured findings and cutting was safer than judging cell by cell.
oracleQuestionInventory.method: Built by programmatic extraction from the source at build time, never retyped: every table cell and quoted block is asserted to be a byte-exact substring of ORACLE_QUESTION_SET.md, and a length tripwire rejects any single extracted run over 2,500 bytes (which is how one anchor collision that would have swallowed 37,776 bytes of measurements was caught before it shipped).

keptDespiteFlag.rule: These files are flagged `mayContainCampaignConclusions: true` and kept anyway. The asymmetry against `trim` is deliberate and is recorded here so it is defensible on the record rather than looking like an oversight.
keptDespiteFlag.reason: The v2-3 figures in the robustness and honesty READMEs — 72.8% re-encode agreement, the ±1-LSB dither moving all 114 test palettes, ~900 tunable sites against 11 human anchors, the 1.61× perturbation-stability ratio — are already in PHASE_1_AUTHOR_BRIEF.md §2 verbatim and deliberately; §2 states outright that they "are here because they define the target, not as a diagnosis of what went wrong". Re-reading them in a README tells an author nothing §2 did not already tell them, so removing them would be theatre. The stats README's figure is a multiplicity-correction methodology illustration and concludes nothing about any palette approach; the adjudication README's numbers are evidence-store inventory of the kind §4 already gives. PERCEPTION_VERDICT.md is the same sanctioned overlap: §3.1 summarises that round at length and names the file as its canonical text.

catalogEntriesWithNoDoc.note: The §5 row is labelled `built` but names no README; it points at `import` from `src/contract/` and `tests/contract-*.test.ts`. The directory holds BELONGS_STUDY.md, PERCEPTION_MODEL_STUDY.md and PERCEPTION_VERDICT.md; none is a README and none was substituted for one. PERCEPTION_VERDICT.md is in the packet on a separate ground — §3.1 names it canonical — not as a stand-in for the missing README.
The §5 row is labelled `built` but names no README; it points at the CLI only. The directory contains no markdown at all. Nothing was substituted.
